https://www.politico.eu/article/emma-bon.text: Italian liberal politician Emma Bonino died Friday at the age of 78 , prompting tributes from across the political spectrum for the civil-rights activist and former European commissioner. “Emma Bonino has represented for decades a strong and recognizable voice of Italian politics, carrying forward her ideas with determination,” said Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni , an ideological foe about whom Bonino was fiercely critical during the 2022 election campaign. “Our stories and our sensibilities have been distant, yet this has never prevented me from recognizing their weight and role in the public life of our nation,” Meloni, who leads the right-wing Brothers of Italy party, added. Advertisement Advertisement A veteran of Italy’s fight for civil and women’s rights, Bonino played a key role in the campaigns that led to the legalization of divorce and abortion in the country during the 1970s. In 2017, she co-founded the liberal More Europe party, which paid tribute to her on Friday. “Activist, parliamentarian, minister, European commissioner. Always radically free,” party leader Riccardo Magi wrote on X . “Her life was a long struggle against everything that denies freedoms.” Carlo Calenda, leader of the liberal Italian Action party, said : “The last great protagonist of the civil battles that led to the modernization of this country,” adding that “a piece of Italian and European political history is passing away.” Bonino’s endeavors extended beyond Italy. She served as a European commissioner in the 1990s, notably overseeing an increase in humanitarian aid to countries and regions affected by some of the most devastating conflicts of the decade, including the Balkans, Rwanda and Afghanistan. “Emma Bonino has never waited for the world to be ready. She has always chosen to move forward, showing the way to others,” wrote European Parliament President Roberta Metsola . “The Europe she fought for will miss her.”

Photograph: Patricia Pinto/Reuters Bolivia Bolivia investigates ex-president Evo Morales over alleged ties to 2009 killings Leftist former leader accused of involvement in shooting of three Europeans in Santa Cruz and torture of two others AFP Mon 12 Oct 2026 17.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Bolivia’s attorney general has announced an investigation into leftist former president Evo Morales , alleging his involvement in the murder and torture of European citizens in 2009. Seventeen years ago, police raided a hotel in the city of Santa Cruz, shooting dead Eduardo Rózsa Flores, a Bolivian-Croatian, Michael Dwyer, an Irishman, and Árpád Magyarosi, a Hungarian-Romanian. Bolivian-Croatian citizen Mario Tadic and Elöd Tóásó from Hungary survived and reported being tortured after their arrest. The Morales administration in power at the time claimed that Rózsa Flores was leading efforts to promote a separatist movement, with funding from the rightwing economic elite of Santa Cruz. Bolivia rocked by protests as US warns of ‘coup d’état’ Read more Acting attorney general José Armando Urioste announced the preliminary investigation into Morales just one week into the job on Monday. In a letter to the supreme court, Urioste said authorities were gathering evidence against Morales and his former vice-president Álvaro García Linera “for the alleged commission of the crimes of murder, abuse, torture and unlawful detention”. The investigation comes after a complaint filed by rightwing lawmakers Tomasa Yarhui and Rodrigo Antonio. When the raid occurred, Morales told the press during an official visit to Venezuela that he had ordered the detention of the foreigners, whom he called “mercenaries”. Family members and victims brought the case before the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, which concluded in 2021 that the government had violated human rights. Neither of the accused has commented on the latest inquiry. Morales, the first-ever Indigenous person to lead Bolivia, is currently in hiding from two active arrest warrants against him. One relates to his alleged role in massive protests that paralysed the country for 53 days earlier this year. The other accuses him of trafficking a minor with whom he is said to have had a daughter. Morales denies the allegations. https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-online-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PFng Prefer DW on Google The shock after the deadly shootings in Krakow runs deep. On social media, this moment is being used to spread misinformation Image: Beata Zawrzel/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement A gunman killed six people in a shooting spree in Krakow's Old Town on Saturday, before being shot and detained by police. The gunman, who is also suspected of killing three family members before the attack, later died in hospital . On Monday, Poland's national prosecutor's office announced a formal investigation . Nevertheless, much is still unknown about the details of the crime, leaving social media users to fill the information vacuum with fake images of the attacker and alleged screenshots of his online profile. DW Fact Check breaks down the developing story. Are these genuine images of the attacker? Claim: A viral picture has been circulating on social media claiming to be the real image of the suspected attacker. DW Fact Check: Fake In the post, the image is posted with the caption, "[…] The perpetrator of the attack in Krakow is a 25-year-old Polish citizen, Polish police have reported. The death toll has reached six. (…)". But the unusual sharpness of this picture raises doubt of its authenticity. It is difficult to imagine capturing such a clear image in a chaotic situation. The footage from X posts about the alleged shooter in Krakow is said to supposedly show the face of the shooter lying on the ground after the attack in Krakow. The face has been altered multiple times with AI Image: X DW checked the image using two different AI detectors. Hive Moderation identified it as 99.5% AI-generated, while Google's SynthID Detector confirmed that it contains a SynthID watermark, indicating that it was generated or edited using Google's AI technology. In our research we found several versions of the suspect image circulating online, most looking very similar. We also found a number of images and videos showing the attack. Although DW cannot independently verify the footage, it shares similarities in terms of the people and background with some original images published by picture agencies. It appears the AI-generated images may have been created using this footage as a reference. Some of the posts sharing these images have also been labeled as AI-generated . One important thing to understand is that AI cannot sharpen a blurry image with correct details or recover details that are not visible in an original photograph. It can generate plausible details based on the surrounding visual information, but these are essentially guesses, not exact reproductions of what was actually there. More about this and how users used sharpening AI tools here . Was the shooter really a supporter of Ukraine? This claim is supposedly backed up by this picture of a post in a Telegram channel Image: X Did the shooter sympathize with Ukraine? Claim: "Michal Oksinski, the terrorist from Krakow who also killed his parents and sister, had a Telegram account with the Ukrainian flag. On November 3, he wrote 'Thanks, Dad, for the gun', posting this photo of himself wearing the Ukrainian flag insignia," an X user wrote in a post viewed more than 700,000 times. DW Fact Check: Fake This Telegram channel is almost certainly inauthentic. The account allegedly posted a photo on November 3, showing the attacker holding a gun, standing in front of a television and a Ukrainian insignia on the wall. Another post on November 4 simply reads, "11/7/2026", the date of the attack. Both of these posts were edited on November 8, after the suspect had been apprehended. DW verified on the Telegram app by hovering over the posts to show the edit history. The channel's photo, a Ukrainian flag, was also edited after the attack took place. Fake: Digital AI tools indicate the image was 99% likely to have been created using AI Image: Hivemoderation.com This is a common disinformation tactic — fake accounts will edit old posts and pictures in the days after a breaking news event to give the appearance that they've predicted or announced the event in advance. Further proof: in Poland, the date is written first, not the month. And the photo of the alleged attacker itself is almost certainly AI-generated. HIVE Moderation said it was 99.9% likely to be created with AI. Does the attacker have links to a group that operated in Ukraine? Claim: "#BREAKING: The attacker in Poland had a full arsenal in this trunk! He also has forward observation group patches, an American military company active in Ukraine," reads an X post viewed nearly 100,000 times. The attached photo of the supposed "arsenal" in the trunk has been shared by several other accounts . DW Fact Check: False The attached photo claims to show the attacker's car with a trunk full of guns, ammunition, a helmet and a military vest. The vest in the trunk of the car features a symbol supposedly connected to the Forward Observations Group, an American tactical training lifestyle brand that has traveled to and operated in Ukraine. This is a photo of a trunk full of weapons — but this picture doesn't show the alleged attacker's car Image: X The patch, however, is the Old Roger flag, a symbol commonly used in military circles. The Forward Observations Group logo is a variation of this symbol, featuring a horned skeleton holding a gun, not an hourglass. This is also not the attacker's car from the scene of the crime. This license plate is registered with the Krakow police, indicating they likely collected evidence from the crime scene and moved it to this car. Little details like these can help separate fact from fiction, especially in a rapidly evolving story like the Krakow shooting. Daniel Ebertz contributed to this article.
